To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

50% of ORF products are covered by protein homology-models, but the coverage of the whole protein structure is still low, that the coverage of prokaryotic ORF products will reach 100% within 15 year, and that the coverage of eukaryotic ORF product will reach 100%, within 25 year.

(1) protein 3D structures are modeled for approximately 50% ORF products in genomes of 276 prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms; (2) the fraction of ORFs with 3D structures is 50% for prokaryotes but 30% for eukaryotes; and (3) the 3D protein structures of soluble proteins in archaebacterial and eubacterial genomes will be available within 15 year, but that

the fraction of the modeled ORF products with 3D structures in the whole genome is approximately 50% in the current FAMBASE, that the fraction will reach 60% in prokaryotes within 15  years and in eukaryote within 25  years, and that the 3D model structures will be for separate domains in ORF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how much of the proteome of each genome can be covered by protein 3D structures and what kind of information we will have at the end of structural genomics.

the following three issues: (i) how to predict disordered regions in ORFs, (ii) how to measure spatial arrangements of structural and disordered regions in single ORFs and (iii) how to measure and predict spatial arrangements of structural regions in multiple ORFs.
the following three points: (i) to predict the 3D structural domains in ORFs, (ii) to measure the spatial arrangements of structural domain in ORFs, and (iii) to predict 3D structures in ORFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are still far from the goal of structural genomics, but we are getting closer to it.
the whole proteome of a genome is not yet covered by 3D structures.

we are now at the beginning of a new phase of structural genomics, which is the structural genomics of structural domains, and we are not yet ready to enter the phase of the structural genomics that deals with entire proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current structural genomics has already started to reveal the whole proteome of prokaryotic species, and that we have to prepare for a next step to reveal the whole eukaryotic proteome.

we are now on the verge of a new era for structural genomics, where structural genomics is not only the determination of protein 3D structures, but the elucidation of spatial arrangements of protein structural domains.
we are in the midst of the transition from a protein structure to a domain structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are on the way to a new era of structural biology, which will provide a complete structural view of the whole proteome.
the 3D protein structure database will not contain the whole ORF products, even after a decade of intensive structural genomics projects.
structural genomics has been progressing at a pace that is faster than we expected, and that the 3D structural models of whole soluble proteins will be in hand soon.
